C-GENERIC-SHAPE-DATA-1-11D2BE52.Problem:
Neo-grace is a generic methodology and CLI for developing other projects; this repository's tests, corpus, CI, and authority records are internal implementation concerns that must not dictate consumer behavior. The pattern detector in `src/review/core.ts` currently contains a private helper `fileHoldsShapesAsData(rel, text)` whose first branch returns `true` whenever `rel.includes("defect-corpus")`; its call site at the detector loop passes the relative path only for that branch. The intended exemption is the explicit file-level marker `@ngrace-review-shape-data`, introduced by correction 88 (`A37.3`/`A38`) to replace an earlier directory-wide `src/review/` prefix exemption. The marker is sound and generic; the surviving `defect-corpus` filename substring branch is not. An arbitrary consumer module named `fixture-defect-corpus-copy.ts`, or any guard living under a `defect-corpus-fixtures/` directory, is silently exempted although it holds a production guard, not fixture data. Measured on the real source CLI, identical unmarked guard bytes under the exact privileged filename, a substring basename, and a substring directory all exit `0` with no finding and a visible exemption; the same bytes under an ordinary path exit `1` with `review.regex-over-structure`. Filename spelling establishes no consumer ownership, so the branch is a publisher-specific bypass inside a generic detector. This bundle removes it.
The original reason for an exemption is not overturned. `A37.3` observed that detector sources legitimately hold the defective shapes as data, and `A38` chose the explicit marker over a path prefix for exactly that reason. A whole-module examination confirms that this repository's `src/test-support/defect-corpus.ts` builds temp projects and injects intentional defective code: the apparent structural predicates inside it are string literals that are written into generated files, not runtime guards. This bundle keeps that module exempt by carrying the sanctioned marker and removes only the filename inference. It does not claim that the archived ruling already prohibited every filename exception; it removes the one that survived the ruling.

Goals.Goal: The pattern detector's shape-data exemption depends on content, never on filename. The same unmarked markup-guard fixture under each specified filename raises `review.regex-over-structure` with severity `error` and rule id `markup-or-attribute-regex-guard` regardless of whether its relative path contains `defect-corpus`: exact filename `defect-corpus.ts`, substring basename `fixture-defect-corpus-copy.ts`, and substring directory `defect-corpus-fixtures/guard.ts` all refuse exactly as an ordinary name does. Only path/finding-id report fields may differ after renaming; code, severity, and pattern identity do not.

The existing explicit marker contract is preserved byte-for-byte. A module whose text contains `SHAPE_DATA_MARKER` (`@ngrace-review-shape-data`) is exempt, appears in the visible `shapeDataExemptions` list and the `summary.shapeDataExemptions` count, and is not flagged, while an adjacent unmarked guard still raises. With fixture data that would otherwise trigger the detector, removing only the marker restores the finding; restoring the exact marker bytes restores the prior report byte-for-byte.

The internal corpus is annotated, not altered. `src/test-support/defect-corpus.ts` gains the existing marker as a comment describing its internal fixture-data role, outside the generated source strings it emits. Its stable defect ids, generated fixture bytes, expected findings, and executable behavior are unchanged, and its existing checks in `src/test-support/defect-corpus.test.ts` continue to pass.

The change is surgical and every preserved boundary is provable: detector rules, the `review.regex-over-structure` code and severity, the report shape, and the scan population (`.ts`/`.js` under `src`, `.test.ts` excluded) are unchanged; no second filename/root exemption, configuration switch, parser redesign, new export, or changed marker syntax is introduced; and the new discriminating filename/marker controls in `src/review/core.test.ts` join the retained generalization, refusal, and exemption reporting checks rather than replacing them.
